subject: HarborTek RFP — Audit Record Retention & Extraction Capabilities
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@harbortek.com>

Cc: Jim O'Leary <jim.oleary@harbortek.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Audit records retention + export questions (HarborTek)

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is a short spreadsheet with 12 specific questions our compliance and forensics teams have about audit records, retention windows, and exportability. We need clear responses for the legal/IT review by next Friday (May 28). High-level asks:

- Maximum configurable retention window for audit logs (per-tenant and system default)
- Support for immutable export snapshots with tamper-evidence
- Formats available for bulk export and incremental deltas
- Chain-of-custody / signatures on exported bundles
- SLA / lead-time for on-demand bulk extracts (>30 days worth, >1TB)

Can you confirm who on your side will own the answers and whether you can supply a sample export playbook or runbook? I've attached the spreadsheet (harbortek_rfp_questions.xlsx).

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement.

Best,
Emily Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
HarborTek Financial

Subject: Re: RFP: Audit records retention + export questions (HarborTek)

Emily —

Thanks for the spreadsheet, we received it and will respond formally. I'll coordinate the response and owner assignment internally and aim to share a draft by May 21. Quick notes:

- Redwood supports per-tenant configurable retention up to 10 years for audit records; default is 1 year. We can scope exceptions for longer retention in contract.
- We can produce export bundles with SHA256 manifests and signed metadata for tamper evidence; the playbook includes our chain-of-custody process.
- Bulk exports can be delivered as compressed NDJSON or Parquet (customer preference), incremental deltas via timestamped slices.
- Typical lead time for large on-demand extracts (~0.5–2TB) is 3–5 business days; emergency expedited delivery available with SLA addendum.

I'm copying Marissa for legal-preservation wording and Ben to coordinate the sample playbook and S3 deliverable.

Regards,

Subject: Fwd: RFP: Audit records retention + export questions (HarborTek)

Forwarding HarborTek's RFP questions. Drafting proposed language below — please review and edit for legal/compliance accuracy before Vanessa sends final.

---DRAFT RESPONSES (summary):
1) Retention windows: configurable per-tenant up to 10 years. Default 365 days. Retention TTLs are policy-enforced and recorded in the system audit ledger.

2) Immutability & tamper-evidence: Exports are produced as a zipped bundle containing NDJSON/Parquet files, a manifest.json with file hashes (SHA256), and a signed provenance certificate. For customers with HSM/KMS, we can sign manifests using a managed key or accept customer-supplied signing keys.

3) Export formats & deltas: Full exports available in NDJSON or Parquet. Incremental exports support timestamped slices and tokenized deltas. Exports include event metadata, actor identity (internal mapping), and session identifiers to preserve traceability.

4) Chain-of-custody: Our export playbook documents the collection, packaging, signing, transfer, and verification steps. We support S3 delivery to customer buckets, direct secure HTTPS transfer, or couriered physical media for very large datasets (rare). Each bundle includes a digest file and an operations manifest.

5) SLA/lead time: Standard delivery 3–7 business days depending on size. For >1TB or >90-day windows we propose a scoped timeline with a committed delivery date; expedited delivery is negotiable.

Action items: Ben to attach the export-playbook-sample.pdf; Kimberly to confirm KMS signing options language and any legal caveats. I'll iterate and return to Vanessa by EOD May 20.

-Marissa

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood response: HarborTek RFP — Audit records retention & extract playbook

Emily / Jim —

Thanks for your patience. Attached are two artifacts to help your review: a completed worksheet with answers (harbortek_rfp_questions.xlsx) and an export-playbook-sample.pdf that shows our packaging/signing/transfer workflow. Key points summarized below and call-out items we think will matter for legal/infosec: 

1) Retention: Per-tenant configurable TTLs up to 10 years. The system records retention policy changes in the configuration audit ledger (immutable entries).

2) Export integrity: Bundles include SHA256 digests for each file and a signed manifest. We can sign manifests with Redwood-managed keys or integrate with customer KMS/HSM for signatures. The playbook describes verification steps for recipients.

3) Formats & slices: Full exports: NDJSON (newline JSON) or partitioned Parquet. Incremental exports available by time-range and event-type; we provide a manifest describing offsets so recipients can reconstruct event order.

4) Delivery & chain-of-custody: Preferred delivery is direct S3 transfer into a customer-controlled bucket with TLS + server-side encryption. We also provide checksums and a signed operations manifest. For high-volume requests we propose a staging window and a mutually agreed delivery date.

5) SLA & timing: Typical turnaround 3–5 business days for up to 1TB. For larger volumes (1–10TB) we propose 5–10 business days; for >10TB or multi-quarter harvests we'll provide a scoped project plan. Expedited delivery and notarization services can be added as contract line-items.

Attachments: harbortek_rfp_questions.xlsx (completed answers); export-playbook-sample.pdf (sample runbook + verification checklist) — both available via secure link: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/evidence/HTK-1147/export-playbook-sample.pdf

Next steps: If this addresses HarborTek's needs we can schedule a 45-minute technical review with our infra & security SMEs next week. Suggest Tue 2027-05-25 or Wed 2027-05-26. Let us know preferred time and any redlines to the retention limits.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
